payload.claim: `_resolve_stacked_on`'s docstring asserts that it and `scheduler._dependency_refusal` 'read the same row the same way,' but `scheduler.py` (states_at_current_sha, per its own comment 'every other state is read only at the sha the spec has on disk now') scopes the waiting-state admission to the parent's *current* `spec_sha`, while `_resolve_stacked_on` pools waiting rows across *every* `spec_sha` the parent has ever carried (via `tasks_by_spec_id`) and takes the newest by `task_id` regardless of which `spec_sha` it belongs to. The two functions are not currently wired together in any live code path, so nothing breaks today, but the claimed equivalence is false whenever a parent has waiting rows recorded under more than one `spec_sha`, and a future caller that trusts this docstring's invariant when wiring an unattended runner would inherit that false assumption.
